title: Entitlement Syncer + Query Gatekeeper for Analytics Views
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Console usage dashboards and ad-hoc analytics require enforcing fine-grained entitlements (org/team/project-level) inside the analytics pipeline. Current approach relied on downstream filtering in the UI which leaks counts and allows accidental access via API. Goal: build a backend-first enforcement path consisting of a near-real-time Entitlement Syncer that converges cloud identity/SCIM/group state into the analytics store and a Query Gatekeeper service that enforces entitlements before queries touch sensitive datasets.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Entitlement Syncer writes user/group→resource grants into analytics_authorization table with <=30s tail for changes. 2) Query Gatekeeper rejects or rewrites queries that would return rows outside caller's grants; no sensitive rows returned in canary runs. 3) Integration tests that exercise SCIM role changes, team deletion, and cross-org queries. 4) Migration plan executed for historical data; alerting and dashboards in place to detect divergence >0.1% between source-of-truth and synced grants.
technical_notes: Design: two components. (A) Entitlement Syncer: streaming consumer of identity change events (SCIM webhooks, internal IAM events) -> transforms to normalized grant tuples -> upserts into analytics_authorization (sharded by org_id). Photo: compact protocol uses protobuf; idempotent apply via (org_id,subject_id,resource_scope,role,valid_from,valid_to). (B) Query Gatekeeper: lightweight service deployed in analytics query path (before planner) that consults authorization cache and either injects WHERE clauses or rejects queries with explicit 'scope' violation. Opt for query rewrite for Presto/Trino-compatible SQL. Caching: TTL-backed in-memory LRU + Redis pubsub invalidation from syncer. Backfill: bulk export of current grants and replay of event log to build initial state. Security: stored grants encrypted at rest; RBAC audit events emitted to kafka topic 'auth-audit'.
tradeoffs: - Enforce in query path (strong security) vs pre-filtering materialized views (faster but more brittle for ad-hoc queries). We choose query gatekeeper to cover ad-hoc workspaces and dashboards. - Tight TTLs reduce staleness but increase cache churn under large org churn; tuned to 30s for most orgs, with option for longer for legacy customers. - Using SQL rewrite keeps analytics engine unchanged but increases complexity around query correctness for complex joins and subqueries.
migration_plan: 1) Run Entitlement Syncer in dry-run mode writing audit rows and metrics. 2) Deploy Gatekeeper in monitoring mode to log would-be-rejections and rewrites. 3) Run canary with 5% of queries for non-sensitive orgs, compare results with baseline. 4) Gradually ramp to 100% after 2 weeks without divergences >0.1%. 5) Backfill authorization table from IAM nightly batch before final cutover.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: 'Auth Sync Lag', 'Gatekeeper Rewrites per minute', 'Auth Divergence Ratio'. Alerts: P0 if sync lag >120s for >5min for any org, P1 if rewrite rejections spike >0.5% of queries, security alert on any rejected query from an internal admin role. Logs: structured audit events to kafka and daily digest to security team.
progress_updates: 2025-11-10: Spike completed. Validated SCIM webhook throughput and protobuf schema prototype (Aisha).
2025-11-20: Prototype Syncer upserts auth tuples into test cluster; observed 95th percentile lag ~18s under synthetic load (Marco).

2025-12-05: Query rewrite approach validated on sample dashboards. Edge cases: window functions and lateral joins required special handling — we implement a pre-planner predicate injection instead of naive string replacement.
2026-01-12: Security review kickoff; noted requirement to encrypt per-org grants and rotate keys — created key rotation subtask (ENG-15102).
2026-01-28: Integration tests flaky for orgs with >10k roles; added pagination and batching to sync apply flow. CI job added to catch regressions.
2026-02-07: Deployed Gatekeeper in monitoring mode to analytics-canary zone; no production rejections observed. Metrics dashboard created: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc123/analytics-auth
2026-02-12: Canaries show 0.03% divergence vs baseline. Plan to start 5% traffic canary for non-sensitive orgs next week.
Next steps: roll out 5% canary, finish key rotation subtask, implement admin override audit endpoint, and schedule compliance sign-off.
review_feedback: PM (Jin Park): prefer conservative default TTLs for enterprise orgs; ensure SLA doc updated.
Design (Sofia Liu): dashboard needs clear explanation of 'divergence' metric and remediation steps.
Security (Ravi Menon): require KMS-backed encryption and per-org access controls for backup exports. Added to security_review_required.
Infra (Olivia Chen): recommend autoscaling Gatekeeper behind ingress with CPU-based horizontal scaling and request throttling to protect analytics cluster.
